events.title: France separates Church and State
events.shortBlurb: The law of 9 December 1905 ended the century-old Concordat between France and the Holy See and opened the age of laïcité…
body: On 9 December 1905 the French Republic passed the law on the Separation of the Churches and the State, ending the Concordat of 1801 by which Napoleon and Pius VII had for more than a hundred years governed the relations of Church and State in France.

The state would no longer recognize or pay the Church, but only associations cultuelles — associations formed in each parish for the conduct of worship; failing such associations, the property of the churches was to be lost forever and handed over to the charitable establishments of the communes. Pope Pius X met the law with resistance: by the encyclical Vehementer Nos of 11 February 1906 he solemnly condemned it as unjust to God and destructive of the Church's rights.

By the encyclical Gravissimo Officii of 10 August 1906 the pope forbade the associations, fearing they would furnish the state a pretext for meddling in the Church's inner life and the laity a constant temptation to rule the parish; the state then treated the old church corporations as nonexistent and transferred their goods, excepting only the edifices still used for worship. The Church of France was stripped of its endowments, and the law of 1905, much amended, still frames French laïcité.
